sources.title: E-Government: Djibouti eVisa
sources.publisher: E-Government Portal / National Agency for State Information Systems, Republic of Djibouti
sources.officialityEvidence: The live E-Government portal says its administrative information is certified by the relevant administrations and identifies ANSIE as a public agency attached to the Presidency. Its visitor eVisa guidance describes approval and email delivery but names no nationalities.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Il remplace le visa délivré au point d'entrée dans le pays.

sources.title: Law No. 201/AN/07/5ème L: entry and stay conditions
sources.publisher: Official Journal of the Republic of Djibouti
sources.officialityEvidence: Djibouti's Official Journal publishes the entry-and-stay law. Its foreign-entry rule is expressly subject to international conventions, bilateral agreements and special regimes, without publishing their nationality scope.
sources.supportingExcerpt: sous réserve des conventions internationales et des accords bilatéraux.

sources.title: Republic of Korea overseas travel safety: Djibouti guide
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Republic of Korea
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Ministry overseas-travel service carries an embassy travel guide for Djibouti, posted 5 June 2024. It describes online and airport routes for a tourist visa, which cannot be reconciled into a stable baseline with Djibouti's current replacement wording.
sources.supportingExcerpt: 온라인 또는 공항 내 도착비자(Visa on arrival)도 신청 가능합니다.

sources.title: Singapore Ministry of Foreign Affairs: Djibouti travel advice
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Singapore MFA Djibouti page is explicitly last updated 24 August 2026. It gives passport-validity advice and refers Singaporeans to Djibouti's embassy for entry information; it does not classify their visitor route.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Travellers are advised to contact your travel agency, or the nearest Embassy of Djibouti.

unresolved.reason: Singapore MFA's current destination page directs travellers to Djibouti's embassy rather than mapping a visitor status. Djibouti's eVisa guidance proves electronic issuance mechanics, not Singapore-passport eligibility; no route is inferred from the fallback.

No current official Swiss or Djiboutian source directly maps an ordinary Swiss passport to a short-visitor issuance route. Djibouti publishes eVisa mechanics but no nationality schedule and preserves bilateral and special regimes.

No current official Finnish or Djiboutian source directly maps an ordinary Finnish passport to a short-visitor issuance route. Djibouti's portal is not nationality eligibility evidence, and the entry law leaves bilateral and special regimes unlisted.

No current official Luxembourg or Djiboutian source directly maps an ordinary Luxembourg passport to a short-visitor issuance route. Neither an eVisa portal nor an unlisted bilateral regime proves the fallback status.

Korea's live official guide describes online and airport tourist-visa applications, while current Djibouti E-Government guidance says eVisa replaces the point-of-entry visa. The sources do not safely establish one current ordinary-passport baseline or issuance timing.

No current official Portuguese or Djiboutian source directly maps an ordinary Portuguese passport to a short-visitor issuance route. The eVisa portal is not proof of eligibility, and no residual rule is published.

No current official Maltese or Djiboutian source directly maps an ordinary Maltese passport to a short-visitor issuance route. Djibouti's electronic channel does not establish eligibility or a nationality-wide baseline.

No current official New Zealand or Djiboutian source directly maps an ordinary New Zealand passport to a short-visitor issuance route. No classification is inferred from the eVisa service or generic foreign-visitor wording.

No current official Greek or Djiboutian source directly maps an ordinary Greek passport to a short-visitor issuance route. The published eVisa process and unlisted bilateral-regime carve-out do not prove the fallback status.

No current official Latvian or Djiboutian source directly maps an ordinary Latvian passport to a short-visitor issuance route. A positive Latvian visa-free list cannot be inverted, and Djibouti supplies no exhaustive residual schedule.

No current official Lithuanian or Djiboutian source directly maps an ordinary Lithuanian passport to a short-visitor issuance route. No portal, omission, regional grouping, or conditional document route is used as evidence.
